title: NevIR: relevance under negation (paired queries and documents)
decision: which of two documents that differ by a negation is relevant to a query

source.name: NevIR: Negation in Neural Information Retrieval (arXiv:2305.07614)

notes: 500 of the 1,383 test instances (seed 20261007), drawn after dropping 1 instance whose two queries are the same string (1314-2); two rows each: the row for q1 has gold A, the row for q2 has gold B; a group counts only if both rows are right, so answering A (or B) on every row scores 0 and independent guessing scores 0.25. Document order is the order of the data in both rows of a group: A = doc1 (the original passage), B = doc2 (the edited passage); the position of the original is therefore constant and a row-level accuracy is not meaningful without the pairing. Queries were written by crowd workers; the documents come from CondaQA. A small training split (948 instances) is public.
